why: Tesla still hasn't set its 2026 annual meeting. Last year's was Nov 6, 2025, and Texas lets a shareholder go to court after 13 months (about Dec 6).

To hold the meeting by Dec 6 with Tesla's usual e-proxy, the notice must go out by about Oct 27. Even mailing full paper sets, Texas needs notice by Nov 26. So a date announcement gets more likely every week from here to late November.

No other public reason for the delay has surfaced, which is why the merger theory fits. But nothing has leaked: no special committee and no bankers, and most deals this big leak first. So the split is roughly even, about 45% with a merger and 55% routine.

Mondays (including Sunday night or pre-market) are the likeliest day, then Tuesdays. Merger-type news should avoid SpaceX unlock days (Oct 26; the Q3-results tranche once SpaceX sets its date) and launches. The Roadster demo (Oct 15) and earnings (Oct 21) are poor days for either.
